title: How Can You Tell if Your AI Agent Skills Are Working?
description:
🚀 Tessl just shipped Agent Skill Support — so what does that actually unlock for you?

In this conversation, Guy breaks down what Tessl’s new agent skill support really means for developers who are already building and using skills. The big shift? Skills stop being loose snippets of prompt text and start behaving like real software artefacts.

You’ll learn how skills can now be:

📦 Packaged, versioned, and published

🧪 Tested and evaluated for quality and effectiveness

🔁 Owned, evolved, and improved over time

📊 Compared objectively using built-in evaluation scores

We also dive into skill evals, a crucial feature when there are tens of thousands of skills to choose from. Tessl automatically evaluates indexed skills and scores them, helping you quickly understand which ones are likely to perform better in your environment.

🧠 Two types of evaluations explained:

Review evals — check whether a skill follows best practices (structure, clarity, activation instructions, and more)

Task evals — run agents with and without a skill to measure how much it actually improves task performance

If you’re serious about building reliable agents and want to know which skills truly move the needle, this is a must-watch.

👉 Explore the skill registry: https://tessl.io/registry

Publish your own skills, discover existing ones, and see how they stack up.
